subject: Re: Aurora (beta) - burst denials + elevated latency today (customer comms + mitigation + hotfix ETA)
related_links: Grafana: Burst Pools / eu-west / Admission Denials (internal)
body:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 9:14 AM -0700
Subject: Aurora (beta) - burst denials + elevated latency today (customer comms + mitigation + hotfix ETA)

Lauren/Jordan/Stephanie,

Escalation from Aurora Support Systems (Dedicated burst beta, eu-west L40S): they saw a sharp increase in burst denials starting ~08:40 PT, plus brief tail latency increase on their baseline route while they attempted a scheduled indexing job.

Customer impact (from Ari’s note + our dashboard screenshots):
- Burst requests admitted rate dropped from ~85–90% to ~30–40% for ~35 minutes
- They hit burst cap and started receiving 429s on their “/chat” high-throughput route (expected when cap is reached, but the timing surprised them)
- They also reported “baseline got slower when burst kicked in” (needs careful phrasing; we should avoid implying noisy-neighbor without evidence)

Asks:
1) Approval on interim mitigation we propose to apply immediately for Aurora (reduce max burst ratio + enforce longer cooldown) while we roll the telemetry smoothing hotfix.
2) Guidance on customer comms: what we commit to on hotfix ETA + whether we offer credits / temporary reserved bump.

Draft customer update is attached (and I can send within 30 mins once we align).

References:
- SUP-28579 (Aurora): burst admission timeouts/denials eu-west
- SUP-28503: 429s when burst cap reached (similar customer education)

—
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success
Redwood Inference


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 9:26 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora (beta) - burst denials + elevated latency today (customer comms + mitigation + hotfix ETA)

Thanks Jasmine.

Yes on interim mitigation for Aurora *if it’s reversible and scoped to tenant + region*. For beta we should bias toward protecting their baseline experience.

On comms: we should say
- we’re seeing elevated denials in eu-west burst pool due to telemetry lag affecting admission decisions
- we’ve applied temporary guardrails for their tenant to stabilize baseline (lower burst ceiling / stricter cooldown)
- we have a hotfix in progress and will update them with rollout timing today

Avoid saying “noisy neighbor” and avoid committing to a precise minute-by-minute ETA unless we have it.

Let’s decide on any credits after we see whether their batch job missed a hard deadline.

Lauren


---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 9:41 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora (beta) - burst denials + elevated latency today (customer comms + mitigation + hotfix ETA)

+1 to Lauren.

Two things I’d like in the customer note:
1) Clarify expected behavior when burst cap is reached: 429s are correct; client should backoff + optional queue behavior is not GA.
2) Make it clear Dedicated baseline allocation remains reserved; bursting is “best effort above baseline” with guardrails.

If they’re in a live launch window, we can offer a temporary reserved uplift (paid or as a one-time exception). Don’t offer credits preemptively in writing.

Jasmine, once you send a draft, I’m happy to do a quick pass.

Jordan


---

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Chen <ari.chen@aurorasupport.com>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@aurorasupport.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 10:08 AM -0700
Subject: Re: [Aurora] Burst beta - increased denials + 429s this morning (eu-west)
Attachments: Draft_customer_update_email_Aurora_2025-04-07.txt

Hi Ari,

Thanks for flagging this quickly — we’re actively investigating.

What we’re seeing on our side:
- Elevated burst admission denials in eu-west this morning, consistent with a telemetry lag issue impacting burst admission decisions.
- When your configured burst cap is reached, the platform will return 429s for requests that would exceed the cap. That part is expected behavior, but we agree the timing and volume of denials today is not what you should see during a normal burst window.

What we’re doing now (interim mitigation):
- We’re applying temporary guardrails to your tenant in eu-west to prioritize baseline stability while we roll a fix. This may reduce peak burst throughput temporarily (i.e., you may see fewer burst admissions), but should prevent the “thrash” behavior you saw this morning.

What’s next / ETA:
- Engineering has a hotfix in progress to address the telemetry-lag edge case (smoothing + guard conditions in the admission controller). We’re targeting validation in staging today and a phased rollout to eu-west thereafter.
- I’ll send you an update with the rollout timing as soon as we have it (today).

In the meantime, if you need to complete the indexing job today, please share:
1) Your latest required completion time
2) A rough request rate / token profile for the job

Based on that, we can recommend the safest way to run it (e.g., spreading over a longer window) and evaluate whether a temporary reserved uplift makes sense.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success | Redwood Inference


---

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 10:12 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora (beta) - burst denials + elevated latency today (customer comms + mitigation + hotfix ETA)
Attachments: Aurora_beta_incident_summary_2025-04-07.docx

I sent a customer-safe update to Ari/Nina (kept it high level, no “noisy neighbor,” no hard ETA). Attached is the incident summary I’m tracking for internal.

Interim mitigation I asked infra to apply (tenant-scoped, eu-west only):
- Temporarily reduce max_burst_ratio from 1.6x -> 1.2x
- Increase cooldown window from 5m -> 15m (reduces oscillation)
- Force stricter circuit-breaker sensitivity for this tenant while telemetry lag is elevated

Open question: Stephanie — Aurora is also in an expansion conversation (moving more traffic to Dedicated). If they ask for guarantees, can you advise what we should/shouldn’t say on “burst availability” during beta?


---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 11:03 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora (beta) - burst denials + elevated latency today (customer comms + mitigation + hotfix ETA)

For beta: we should not promise burst availability as an SLA.

If they push for guarantees:
- Baseline Dedicated capacity is reserved and SLA-backed (per contract)
- Burst is designed to be “best effort above baseline” with guardrails; availability can vary with pool headroom
- For guaranteed peak throughput, we recommend increasing reserved baseline (and we can do temporary uplifts for known events)

If Aurora needs a commitment for a near-term event, route that through me and Lauren so we don’t create a one-off promise.


---

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Chen <ari.chen@aurorasupport.com>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@aurorasupport.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 1:58 PM -0700
Subject: Re: [Aurora] Burst beta - increased denials + 429s this morning (eu-west)

Hi Ari,

Quick update as promised:

- We applied a temporary configuration change for your tenant in eu-west to reduce burst admission oscillation and keep baseline stable (this lowers the peak burst ceiling temporarily).
- The engineering hotfix for the telemetry-lag edge case is now in final validation. Assuming validation stays clean, we’re targeting rollout to eu-west in the next deployment window today, with monitoring immediately after.

Two questions so we can align on the best plan for your indexing job:
1) Are you planning to re-run the job today? If yes, what time window?
2) Are you okay with a smoother-but-lower peak (more predictable throughput), or do you need the highest possible peak even if we risk more denials?

Once I have that, I can recommend the safest settings while the hotfix is rolling out.

Best,
Jasmine
